s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive systemic illness with unintentional weight loss and fatigue, accompanied by pancytopenia and a cardiac mass
salient_findings: Months of fatigue and 20-pound unintentional weight loss
Pancytopenia with subsequent recovery of all cell lines
Cardiac mass encasing the mid-right coronary artery
key_facts: 83-year-old man
History of colon cancer treated with surgery and 5-fluorouracil
History of squamous cell carcinoma of the right palatine tonsil treated with radiation
History of squamous cell carcinoma and basal cell carcinoma of the skin
Family history of various cancers without clear genetic cause
Initial laboratory evaluation revealed new pancytopenia
Complete blood count showed pancytopenia with subsequent recovery
Peripheral blood smear showed no peripheral blasts or abnormal B or T cells
Flow cytometry of tissue blasts was positive for CD13, CD34, CD38, and CD117
CT scan showed patchy enhancement of right palatine tonsil
PET-CT revealed hypermetabolic cervical lymph nodes and an ill-defined focus near the inferior right atrioventricular groove
Cardiac MRI showed a mass with heterogeneous signal intensity and postcontrast enhancement
Transthoracic echocardiogram showed a mass within the right atrium, causing restricted anterior tricuspid leaflet motion and mild tricuspid stenosis
Endomyocardial biopsy showed 80% tissue blast cells

shortlist.label: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: Flow cytometry of tissue blasts was positive for CD13, CD34, CD38, and CD117, and endomyocardial biopsy showed 80% tissue blast cells

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of various cancers, hypermetabolic cervical lymph nodes on PET-CT, and cardiac mass with heterogeneous signal intensity on MRI

shortlist.label: Metastatic Disease
shortlist.why_kept: History of colon cancer, squamous cell carcinoma of the right palatine tonsil, and squamous cell carcinoma and basal cell carcinoma of the skin, with a cardiac mass on imaging

shortlist.label: Cardiac Sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cardiac mass with heterogeneous signal intensity and postcontrast enhancement on MRI, and mass encasing the mid-right coronary artery on CT angiography

shortlist.label: Waldenstrom Macroglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Pancytopenia with subsequent recovery, and history of various cancers without clear genetic cause

raw.rationale: The patient's initial laboratory evaluation revealed new pancytopenia, which later showed recovery of all cell lines, and flow cytometry of tissue blasts was positive for CD13, CD34, CD38, and CD117, which are markers commonly associated with Acute Myeloid Leukemia. Additionally, the endomyocardial biopsy showed 80% tissue blast cells, further supporting this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: The peripheral blood smear showed no peripheral blasts or abnormal B or T cells, and the fine needle aspiration of cervical lymph node showed normal reactive tissue, making Lymphoma less likely.

rejected.label: Metastatic Disease
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of various cancers, the presence of blast cells in the endomyocardial biopsy and the specific markers on flow cytometry suggest a primary hematologic malignancy rather than metastatic disease.

rejected.label: Cardiac Sarcoma
rejected.why: The cardiac MRI and transthoracic echocardiogram did show a mass within the right atrium, but the presence of blast cells and specific markers on flow cytometry are more indicative of a hematologic malignancy than a primary cardiac sarcoma.

rejected.label: Waldenstrom Macroglobulinemia
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with anemia, thrombocytopenia, and an elevated IgM level, which were not mentioned in the case report, making it less likely than Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
